card.name: Linking words in vision-loss warnings
card.fires_on: Small linking words or punctuation (of, (, to, and) right after a vision-loss term such as decreased vision, optic neuropathy, myopia or blindness, in warnings about eye problems.

modes.label: Link after eye condition
modes.description: An 'and', '(' or 'of' follows an eye condition name, just before an abbreviation or the next eye condition.
modes.example: resulting in acute transient myopia<< and>> acute angle-closure glaucoma.

modes.label: Parenthesis after optic neuropathy
modes.description: An opening parenthesis follows non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, ahead of the abbreviation NAION.
modes.example: Non–arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy<< (>>NAION), a cause of decreased vision

modes.label: Link in vision-loss phrase
modes.description: A linking word sits inside a phrase about worsening vision or blindness.
modes.example: abnormal vision from blurriness<< to>> blindness, associated or not with hypertension [

card.writes: Weakly favors abbreviation-like tokens starting with LP; the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words right after eye and vision-loss terms in drug warnings.
